exact_authored_statement_excerpt:
statement: >-
  Every Coach instance is called "Coach - <project or repo>" in its window or tab label, its session
  title and the first line of every report it writes, so the owner can tell which repository a Coach
  serves.

statement: >-
  Every decision a Coach takes falls into one of four tiers: act alone, act then report, ask the owner
  first, or never. The tier comes from the action's kind and its reach, not from how confident the
  Coach feels that the action is safe.

statement: >-
  Each decision a Coach takes alone (act alone, or act then report) is written to a decision log with the
  request, the tier, the convention that applies and the evidence, in the same step as the action or before it.

statement: >-
  A request that is small, reversible and already covered by an active convention or a standing approval
  is handled by the Coach without asking the owner. The Coach records the decision and reports it in one line.

statement: >-
  When a Coach cannot place an action in one tier, or cannot tell whether it is reversible or stays inside
  its own repository, it applies the higher of the candidate tiers. An action does not drop a tier because
  it looks small.

statement: >-
  A Coach orchestrates work: it grants and routes, checks evidence, validates merge readiness and reviews
  exceptionally. It never edits repository code and never opens a code pull request itself. Code is
  produced by a worker under a brief and a tracked issue.

statement: >-
  A coder who pushes a branch or opens a pull request for a code change puts the tracker issue id in
  the branch name and in the PR body, and keeps the issue status current: In Progress when the work
  starts, Done when its acceptance is met, and an explicit comment when it is blocked.

statement: >-
  A planner extends the local plan binding with the external tracker: before a decomposition is
  ratified, it is bound to a local ATDD issue (planner.plan.confirm-binds-an-issue) and that issue is
  linked to an issue in the configured tracker, so the owner sees the planned code work before any
  repository change starts.

statement: >-
  When an agent meets a situation no active convention covers, or an active convention that misfires,
  it records a convention proposal and continues its assigned work under the conventions that are
  active now. An agent never creates, edits, disables or deletes an active convention itself. A
  proposal carries concrete evidence, names the profile and area the rule belongs to, and is never
  applied to the task in which it was raised. Gaps found by experiments enter through the same path.

statement: >-
  An automatic context handoff MUST fire at most once per threshold crossing, MUST be latched at the
  crossing rather than cancelled by usage read later (Pi may compact first), MUST be dropped only when
  the run was aborted, and MUST stop at a configured hop limit. A failed or cancelled session switch
  MUST keep the record for a manual retry and MUST NOT retry on its own.

statement: >-
  A context handoff record MUST carry only bounded facts: the issue id, the workspace and revision,
  the usage at the threshold crossing, the task text with values under listed credential labels and token
  shapes redacted on a best-effort basis, and explicit `UNKNOWN` markers for anything not known. Redaction
  is list-based and is not general secret safety; it does not make a prompt safe to repeat. It MUST NOT copy the predecessor's own output, and it MUST
  NOT present any claimed completion as evidence. Its grant is stated by reference to the original brief.
  When the handing-off session is a Coach, the record MAY also carry an optional `Coach state` section under
  the s

statement: >-
  A worker escalates one tier only after two failures on the same task, and only after reporting both
  failures with their evidence. Escalation is never silent. A step to `high` or `xhigh` still needs an
  explicit owner request for the named task.

statement: >-
  Briefs, rules, configs and repository files name a tier (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`), never a
  model name, a model id or a hard-coded `--model` flag. The configured tiers file is the only place
  where a tier becomes a provider, model and thinking level.

statement: >-
  Agents run only on the subscription provider families configured in the tiers file. Per-token
  providers (anthropic, openai) are never used for agents unless the owner asks for them by name.
  Switching provider family is the owner's call, and the agent asks for it only through its Coach; it is
  never silent. When a family reaches its limit, the agent reports it and stops or waits rather than
  falling back to another provider.

statement: >-
  When an agent launches another agent or a worker, it chooses the model by tier from its role:
  planners, testers, coders and bounded-task operators run on `low`; coordinators and coaches run on `medium`, and
  `high` or `xhigh` are used only on an explicit owner request for a named task. The brief names the
  tier; the tiers file decides the provider, model and thinking level.

statement: >-
  A code change (repository file, CI, deploy/infra or cloud build config) MUST be bound to an issue in
  the configured tracker before its first change. No issue: ask the owner, or create one only with approval.
  The issue id goes in the branch name and PR body; the issue stays current until the work is done.

statement: >-
  With no tracker configured, a code change cannot be bound to a tracker issue: say so explicitly in the
  report and check result. Never report it as tracked, never pass it silently, never invent a tracker or id.

statement: >-
  A repository that still uses a legacy railway term (wagon, train, interlocking, Cargo, WMBT,
  Station Master) migrates it with the mapping table in conventions/legacy-terms.yaml. Prose in a file
  the agent is already editing takes the new term in the same commit. Identifiers (rule ids, paths,
  URN schemes, field keys, code names) migrate as a whole unit with the mechanical tool, because their
  references live in other files and other repositories. Until then the alias keeps the legacy name
  resolving. The vocabulary change is its own commit, and no file keeps both vocabularies after its unit
  is migrated. Advisory until the sunset date (60 days after the release that sh

statement: A file under a design root MUST NOT import a relative path that resolves outside the design root. Product capabilities
  and app code import FROM the design system, never the reverse, so the system stays capability-agnostic. Bun realization
  of the outward half of `coder.design.hierarchy-import`, mirroring `coder.vite.design-capabilities-import`.

statement: An app component (`.tsx`/`.jsx` outside the design root) that renders markup MUST import at least one
  design-system element — token, primitive, component, or template — so no UI surface is disconnected from the shared
  system. Bun realization of `coder.design.orphan-ui`.

statement: A file under a design root MUST import only from its own layer or a lower one in the hierarchy tokens/foundations
  (0) <- primitives (1) <- components (2) <- templates (3). Upward edges — tokens importing primitives, primitives
  importing components, components importing templates — are forbidden. Bun realization of the core obligation `coder.design.hierarchy-import`,
  mirroring `coder.vite.design-dependency-flow`.

statement: >-
  A module MUST import only inward: presentation -> application -> domain; integration -> application,
  domain; assembly (the composition root) may reach any layer. Bun realization mirroring
  `coder.convex.design-hierarchy-import`; core obligation `coder.backend.imports-respect-dependency-
  allowed`.

statement: Every component a `primitives`, `components`, or `templates` file exports MUST be imported by at least
  one other file — a higher design layer or app code — so the system stays lean. Re-exports through an `index.*`
  barrel are not consumption. Bun realization of `coder.design.orphan-export`, counting consumers the way `coder.vite.design-orphan-ui`
  does, so composition inside the system (a template using a component) is legitimate.

statement: >-
  A module in the `domain/`, `application/` or `presentation/` layer MUST NOT call the platform `fetch()`
  primitive or a bare `axios` call; outbound HTTP goes through the project's centralized, contract-driven
  client. Bun realization mirroring `coder.vite.boundaries-http-client`; core obligation
  `coder.boundaries.http-client`.

statement: >-
  A product capability document declares a DATA CONTRACT: `produce[]` are the artifacts the product capability owns and
  `consume[]` the ones it takes from other product capabilities (core `capability.schema.json` requires both). The Bun
  implementation MUST name each declared artifact where it moves flow variables, so the declaration and the
  data actually carried cannot drift apart. Core validates that the contract is well formed; only a
  per-stack detector can see whether this stack's code honours it.

statement: >-
  A module under a `commons/application/` or `shared/application/` tree MUST NOT import from the commons
  `integration/` layer. Bun realization mirroring `coder.convex.commons-application-no-integration`; core
  obligation `coder.commons.domain-layer-purity`.

statement: >-
  A module at `commons/<layer>/<feature>/…` MUST NOT import directly into a SIBLING feature's internals;
  cross-feature use goes through the layer root. Bun realization mirroring `coder.convex.commons-cross-
  feature-imports-in`; core obligation `coder.boundaries.no-cross-capability-imports`.

statement: >-
  A module in the `domain/` layer MUST NOT import runtime machinery (`bun:*`, `node:*`, `htmx`, `express`,
  `fastify`, `koa`) nor reach the `Bun.` global. Bun realization mirroring `coder.vite.commons-domain-no-
  framework-import`; core obligation `coder.commons.domain-layer-purity`.

statement: >-
  A module under a `commons/domain/` or `shared/domain/` tree MUST NOT import from the commons
  `application/` or `integration/` layers. Bun realization mirroring `coder.convex.commons-domain-no-
  outbound`; core obligation `coder.commons.domain-layer-purity`.

statement: >-
  Every TypeScript/TSX function MUST keep its cyclomatic complexity at or below 10, so the number of
  independent paths through any one function stays testable. Stack-neutral obligation, NATIVE BUN
  detector: the thresholds and the counting rule are transcribed from the python-pytest sibling
  `coder.refactor.complexity-cyclomatic-typescript` and verified to produce identical numbers, so this
  repo enforces its own metrics without a Python interpreter. Realized by `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core
  alias COMPLEXITY-CYCLOMATIC-TS-001).

statement: >-
  Every TypeScript/TSX function MUST be at most 50 lines of code, excluding blank and comment lines.
  Stack-neutral obligation, NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-pytest sibling
  `coder.refactor.complexity-length-typescript` and verified numerically identical. Realized by
  `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core alias COMPLEXITY-LENGTH-TS-001).

statement: >-
  Every TypeScript/TSX function MUST keep its maximum control-flow nesting depth at or below 4. Stack-
  neutral obligation, NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-pytest sibling
  `coder.refactor.complexity-nesting-typescript` and verified numerically identical. Realized by
  `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core alias COMPLEXITY-NESTING-TS-001).

statement: >-
  A module in the `presentation/` or `application/` layer MUST receive its collaborators by injection
  rather than constructing them. Bun realization mirroring `coder.convex.composition-consumer`; core
  obligation `coder.refactor.composition-consumer`.

statement: >-
  Instantiation of a feature's collaborators (`*Repository`, `*Client`, `*Service`, `*Adapter`,
  `*Gateway`, `*Store`, `*Provider`, `*Factory`) MUST happen only in a composition root —
  `composition.ts`, `capability.ts`, `server.ts`, `index.ts`. Bun realization mirroring
  `coder.convex.composition-root`; core obligation `coder.refactor.composition-root`.

statement: >-
  Every TypeScript/TSX file MUST be reachable, forwards or backwards, from a structural root (`index`,
  `capability`, `composition`, `main`, `app`) through the module import graph. Stack-neutral obligation, NATIVE
  BUN detector; the traversal and root vocabulary are transcribed from the python-pytest sibling
  `coder.dead-code.reachability-typescript`, but the import graph is built by Bun's in-process TypeScript
  parser rather than by regex. Realized by `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core alias DEAD-CODE-REACHABILITY-
  TS-001).

statement: >-
  A function mapping between a DTO and a domain entity (`to*DTO`, `from*DTO`, `map*DTO*`) MUST live in the
  `integration/` layer. Bun realization mirroring `coder.convex.dto-mapper`; core obligation
  `coder.dto.mapper`.

statement: >-
  A `*DTO` type MUST be declared inside a `contracts/` module, not inside a feature's internal layer. Bun
  realization mirroring `coder.convex.dto-placement`; core obligation `coder.dto.placement`.

statement: >-
  A `*DTO` type or interface MUST have no method members and no non-`readonly` fields. Bun realization
  mirroring `coder.convex.dto-purity`; core obligation `coder.dto.purity`.

statement: >-
  No run of 7 or more non-trivial normalized lines may appear in two different TypeScript files of the
  SAME architectural layer. Stack-neutral obligation, NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-
  pytest sibling `coder.duplication.no-intra-layer-code-typescript`, including the normalization table and
  the sha256-prefix fingerprint. Realized by `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core alias DUPLICATION-TS-001).

statement: >-
  A `Response` with a 4xx or 5xx status MUST NOT have a bare string literal as its body; it MUST carry a
  structured payload with an error code. Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest
  sibling matches FastAPI's `HTTPException(detail="...")`, which does not exist here — a Bun error IS a
  `Response` with a status. Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias ERROR-BARE-
  STRING-001).

statement: >-
  An `error_code` value MUST be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. Stack-neutral obligation, and the second of only two
  rules in this family that PORTS verbatim: the payload is JSON, so the pattern and the case test carry
  over from the python-pytest sibling `coder.error-response.code-format` unchanged. Realized by
  `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias ERROR-CODE-FORMAT-001).

statement: >-
  A flow router system is systemic, not descriptive: it requires CLOSURE across declaration (the
  flow router YAML route space, core afokapu/atdd#1248), runtime resolution (FlowRouterRunner,
  core afokapu/atdd#1251), journey router reachability (the `server.ts` JOURNEY_MAP), FlowRunner
  delegation, and the execution trace. This convention binds those surfaces in FIVE directions so a
  declared route, a runtime resolution, a journey router action, and a recorded trace can never drift
  apart silently. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `coder.user-system-flow.flow-router-bilateral-binding`; the JS detector `bun_flow_router_binding` realizes

statement: >-
  An `FlowRouterRunner` MUST NOT execute product capabilities directly or duplicate the FlowRunner step loop. The
  FlowRouterRunner-defining module MUST NOT import a `src/<capability>/capability.ts` module, call
  `runUserSystemFlow(...)`, loop over `<expr>.sequence` as an executor, or otherwise invoke product capability steps;
  FlowRunner remains the only capability-step executor. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic
  core obligation `coder.user-system-flow.flow-router-delegates-to-flowrunner` (core afokapu/atdd#1251); the JS
  detector that enforces it is the atdd.workspace.bun implementation referenced below.

statement: >-
  Flow variables are the artifact data plane carried by FlowRunner between product capabilities inside a selected user/system flow. An
  `FlowRouterRunner` MUST NOT reference or mutate flow variables, MUST NOT store `artifact_urn -> artifact_data`
  runtime values, and MUST NOT route on mid-user/system-flow flow-variable state; and Bun product capabilities (`src/<capability>/capability.ts`)
  MUST NOT import flow router code. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `coder.user-system-flow.flow-router-does-not-carry-flow-variables` (core afokapu/atdd#1251); the JS detector that enforces
  it is the atdd.workspace.bun implementation referenced below.

statement: >-
  An `FlowRouterRunner.resolveUserSystemFlow(...)` MUST resolve a structured `FlowRouterResolution` model
  carrying the route metadata — not a bare `userSystemFlowId` string. The model MUST define the fields
  `flowRouterId`, `routeId`, `userSystemFlowId`, `userSystemFlowPath`, `category`, `guardId`, `resolutionStrategy`, and
  `reason`. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `coder.user-system-flow.flow-router-resolution-model-exists` (core afokapu/atdd#1251); the JS detector that
  enforces it is the atdd.workspace.bun implementation referenced below.

statement: >-
  When a consumer Bun application declares guarded flow router routes (a `JOURNEY_MAP` entry that is an
  `{flowRouterId, path}` route object in the journey router composition root `server.ts`), the
  consumer runtime MUST ship an `FlowRouterRunner` route-control layer — a `class FlowRouterRunner`
  defined under `src/user-system-flows/**` that exposes a `resolveUserSystemFlow(...)` entry point. This is the
  Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation `coder.user-system-flow.flow-router-runner-exists`
  (core afokapu/atdd#1251, Part of #1246); the zero-dependency JS detector that enforces it is the
  atdd.workspace.bun implementation referenced below.

statement: >-
  Where present, header fields MUST appear as URN -> Tested-By -> Runtime -> Purpose. Stack-neutral
  obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-
  HEADER-004).

statement: >-
  Every implementation file MUST carry a `Purpose:` description of at most 80 characters. Stack-neutral
  obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-
  HEADER-002).

statement: >-
  Every implementation file MUST carry a `Runtime:` declaration naming `bun`, `browser` or `isomorphic`.
  Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific vocabulary; realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core
  alias GREEN-HEADER-001).

statement: >-
  Every implementation file MUST carry a `Tested-By:` block containing at least one `- test:…` acceptance
  URN. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector`
  (core alias GREEN-HEADER-003).

statement: >-
  The `{capability}` and `{feature}` segments of a URN MUST match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. Stack-neutral
  obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-
  URN-003).

statement: >-
  The `{layer}` segment of a URN MUST be one of `domain`, `application`, `integration`, `presentation`,
  `assembly`. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized by
  `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-URN-006).

statement: >-
  A Bun/htmx implementation file — `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.mts` AND `.html`/`.htm`
  template — MUST carry a `URN: component:…` marker as its first meaningful line. Stack-neutral obligation
  (required in every implementation file), Bun-specific dual-syntax detector: `// URN:` in source, `<!--
  URN: … -->` in a template. The Python realization writes `# URN:` and the Vite one `// URN:`; this is
  the same obligation with a third comment syntax. Realized by the family validator
  `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-URN-001).

statement: >-
  The `{Name}` segment of a URN MUST match the file's basename, compared case- and separator-
  insensitively, unless the name is a structural role. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector;
  realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-URN-004).

statement: >-
  A `URN:` marker MUST read `component:{capability}:{feature}:{Name}:{side}:{layer}` — literal `component`
  first, then exactly five non-empty segments. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector; realized
  by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-URN-002).

statement: >-
  The `{side}` segment of a URN MUST be `frontend` or `backend`. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific
  detector; realized by `bun_green_traceability_detector` (core alias GREEN-URN-005).

statement: >-
  A template literal that emits HTML MUST NOT interpolate a bare variable or property chain
  (`${user.name}`) directly into the markup; the value MUST pass through an escaping helper first. In a
  full-stack Bun + htmx application the server renders fragments as template literals and htmx inserts
  them into the live DOM via `innerHTML`, so there is no framework auto-escaping anywhere in the path.
  This is the Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "untrusted data is escaped at the rendering
  boundary" obligation, enforced by the `htmx_hypermedia_detector` family implementation on
  `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  Markup that uses htmx MUST NOT carry inline HTML event handlers (`onclick="…"`, `onsubmit="…"`,
  `onchange="…"`, …). Behaviour in a hypermedia application is declared with `hx-trigger` and `hx-on`,
  which participate in htmx's event and swap lifecycle; an inline handler does not. This is the
  Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "behaviour is declared where the framework can see it"
  obligation, enforced by the `htmx_hypermedia_detector` family implementation on
  `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  Every element carrying `hx-swap-oob` MUST also carry an `id`. htmx matches an out-of-band element to
  its destination BY ID; an oob element with no id has no destination, so htmx discards it silently —
  no error, no console warning, no swap. This is the Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic
  "a declarative binding must name its target" obligation, enforced by the `htmx_hypermedia_detector`
  family implementation on `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  Every element carrying `hx-delete` MUST also carry `hx-confirm` (or `hx-prompt`). In a hypermedia
  application a delete is one attribute on a clickable element: there is no form submit, no route
  transition and no framework guard between the user's click and the destructive request.
  `hx-confirm` IS that guard, and it is declarative precisely so it cannot be forgotten. This is the
  Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "a destructive action requires explicit intent"
  obligation, enforced by the `htmx_hypermedia_detector` family implementation on
  `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  An endpoint declared by a STATE-CHANGING htmx verb (`hx-post`, `hx-put`, `hx-patch`, `hx-delete`)
  MUST be served by the journey router surface — the module declaring the `JOURNEY_MAP`. htmx
  declares its route space in the MARKUP, which is what makes it hypermedia; without this, that
  markup can mint a state-advancing route the journey space never admitted, and the affordance posts
  into nothing.

statement: >-
  Every htmx verb attribute (`hx-get`, `hx-post`, `hx-put`, `hx-patch`, `hx-delete`) MUST address a
  same-origin path (`/api/orders`) and MUST NOT carry a hardcoded absolute or protocol-relative URL
  (`https://host/…`, `//host/…`). htmx swaps the response body directly into the live DOM, so the
  endpoint's origin is a trust boundary, not a configuration detail. This is the Bun/htmx-stack
  realization of the agnostic "a client must not hardcode a foreign origin" obligation; the detector
  that enforces it is the `htmx_hypermedia_detector` family implementation on
  `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  Every element issuing a mutating htmx request (`hx-post`, `hx-put`, `hx-patch`, `hx-delete`) MUST
  declare either `hx-indicator` or `hx-disabled-elt`. htmx swaps in place with no navigation, so
  without one of these the page is visually identical while the request is in flight: the user
  receives no feedback, clicks again, and a non-idempotent request runs twice. This is the
  Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "an in-flight mutation is observable" obligation, enforced
  by the `htmx_hypermedia_detector` family implementation on `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  The journey router composition root (`server.ts`) MUST support both direct user/system flow routing and
  flow-router-enabled routing: its `JOURNEY_MAP` MUST admit a direct `userSystemFlowId` string AND an
  `{flowRouterId, path}` route object, and when a flow router route is present the journey router MUST
  reference `FlowRouterRunner` and ultimately reference `FlowRunner` for the selected user/system flow. This is
  the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `coder.user-system-flow.journey-router-flow-router-routing` (core afokapu/atdd#1251); the JS detector that
  enforces it is the atdd.workspace.bun implementation referenced below.

statement: >-
  Every journey document with entrypoint.exposed=true MUST be reachable from the Bun journey router
  composition root. Each declared entrypoint action MUST appear in server.ts JOURNEY_MAP as a
  {journeyId, path} mapping to that journey document, and the journey router MUST reference
  JourneyRunner. Internal journeys (entrypoint.exposed=false) carry no journey router reachability
  obligation. This closes the public entry direction for the higher-order journey topology without
  weakening the existing direct-user/system-flow or direct-flow-router mappings.

statement: >-
  A Bun consumer that declares one or more journey topology documents under plan/_journeys/ MUST ship
  a JourneyRunner under src/user-system-flows/**. JourneyRunner is the continuation-control layer above
  FlowRouterRunner: it MUST read and parse the declared journey topology, MUST reference
  FlowRouterRunner for routing decisions, MUST NOT construct a FlowRouterRunner from a hardcoded
  literal path, and MUST NOT bypass
  that boundary by referencing FlowRunner directly, importing product capability modules, calling runUserSystemFlow(...),
  looping over user-system-flow.sequence as an executor, or carrying/mutating flow variables. FlowRouterRunner continues
  to select exa

statement: >-
  A module inside a `features/` or `capabilities/` tree MUST name its architectural layer — either by filename
  (`domain.ts`, `application.ts`, `api.ts`, …) or by living in a directory named for the layer. Bun
  realization mirroring `coder.convex.layer-naming`; core obligation `coder.backend.code-is-organized`.

statement: >-
  Application source MUST NOT call `console.log` / `info` / `warn` / `error` / `debug` / `trace` / `dir`.
  Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest sibling walks the AST for a bare
  `print(...)`; the Bun equivalent is `console.*`. Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias
  LOGGING-PRINT-001).

statement: >-
  A logger call MUST NOT pass only a bare string; it MUST carry a context object. Stack-neutral
  obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the receiver names and log methods carry over from the python-pytest
  sibling `coder.logging.structured`, but the argument shape does not — a JS logger takes a context OBJECT
  where the Python one takes `extra=` or kwargs. Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias
  LOGGING-STRUCTURED-001).

statement: >-
  During governed coding work, GREEN MUST target the smallest correct implementation that makes the current
  behavioral acceptance pass while respecting active construction constraints. REFACTOR begins only after
  behavioral GREEN and uses quality findings as design sensors. Phase ordering never waives strict
  enforcement: review-ready work MUST pass all active profiles.

statement: >-
  Every TypeScript/TSX file MUST have a comment ratio of at least 10% of non-blank lines. Stack-neutral
  obligation, NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-pytest sibling `coder.refactor.quality-
  comments-typescript` and verified numerically identical. Realized by `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core
  alias REFACTOR-QUALITY-COMMENTS-TS-001).

statement: >-
  Every TypeScript/TSX file MUST score at least 20 on the approximate SEI maintainability index. Stack-
  neutral obligation, NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-pytest sibling
  `coder.refactor.quality-mi-typescript` — the Halstead volume, the log terms and the comment term are the
  same formula, verified identical to ten decimal places. Realized by `bun_ts_metrics_detector` (core
  alias REFACTOR-QUALITY-MI-TS-001).

statement: Every width condition in an `@media` query, `min-width`/`max-width` or the range syntax (`width >= 768px`,
  `768px <= width`), MUST use one of the breakpoints declared under `frontend.breakpoints` in `atdd-bun.yaml` (default
  480, 768, 1024, 1280). A `max-width` within 1px below a breakpoint (`767px`, `767.98px`) counts as that breakpoint,
  and `em`/`rem` convert at 16px. New in atdd-bun, strict.

statement: A `width` or `min-width` declaration, in a stylesheet, a `<style>` block, a `style` attribute or a JSX
  `style` object, MUST NOT exceed (with `rem` and `em` counted at 16px) the smallest viewport declared under `frontend.viewports`
  in `atdd-bun.yaml` (default 375px). New in atdd-bun, strict.

statement: Every full HTML document (an `.html`/`.htm` file, a `.tsx`/`.jsx` layout that renders `<html>`, or a
  `.ts`/`.js` template that builds one) MUST declare `<meta name="viewport">` whose content sets `width=device-width`,
  and MUST NOT block zoom with `user-scalable=no` or a `maximum-scale` below 2. New in atdd-bun, strict.

statement: >-
  A consumer that declares guarded flow router routes MUST have a runtime that READS the
  declaration it is given. An `FlowRouterRunner` constructed with a flow router YAML path MUST
  load that path and resolve from what it read; a `FlowRunner` MUST take the product capability order from the
  user/system flow definition. A runtime that stores the path and returns hardcoded values satisfies every
  text-level rule in this package and is not executing the plan — it is transcribing it.

statement: >-
  A full-stack Bun application MUST serve HTTP with `Bun.serve` and MUST NOT construct a server with
  Express, Fastify, Koa or `node:http`/`node:https` `createServer`. `Bun.serve` is the only server in
  this stack with access to Bun's native routing, WebSocket upgrade, streaming and `HTMLRewriter` —
  the last of which is how htmx fragments are transformed server-side. This is the Bun-stack
  realization of the agnostic "the application uses its runtime's native primitives rather than a
  compatibility shim" obligation, enforced by the `bun_fullstack_detector` family implementation on
  `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  A repository whose package manager is Bun MUST NOT carry `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock` or
  `pnpm-lock.yaml` alongside `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb`. Two lockfiles mean two resolvers disagree about
  the dependency graph, and which one wins is decided by whichever command a developer or CI step
  happens to run. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic "dependency resolution has one
  source of truth" obligation, enforced by the `bun_fullstack_detector` family implementation on
  `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  A Bun project containing TypeScript sources MUST have a typechecker it can run and MUST wire a
  no-emit typecheck into its check path — TypeScript (or an equivalent native preview) as a
  dependency, a `tsconfig.json`, and some script that runs a no-emit typecheck. Bun executes `.ts`
  by STRIPPING types; it transpiles and never checks, and it bundles no `tsc`. Absent this, a Bun
  stack is by default less type-safe than a tsc-based one.

statement: >-
  Source MUST NOT contain a secret literal — an AWS access key id, a PEM private-key header, or a password
  / api-key / token assigned a literal string. Stack-neutral obligation, and one of only two rules in this
  family that PORTS verbatim: the five patterns in the python-pytest sibling `coder.security.hardcoded-
  secret` are language-neutral, because `password = "..."` and a PEM header look identical in Python and
  TypeScript. Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias SECURITY-HARDCODED-SECRET-001).

statement: >-
  A route handler for POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE MUST perform an authorisation check in its body. Stack-
  neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest sibling matches a FastAPI decorator whose
  signature carries `Depends(get_current_user)`. Bun has neither decorators nor a DI container — routes
  are entries in the `routes` object of `Bun.serve` or branches of a `fetch` handler, and authorisation is
  an ordinary call. Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias SECURITY-MISSING-AUTH-001).

statement: >-
  SQL passed to a query sink MUST NOT be built by interpolating a template literal or concatenating
  strings. Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest sibling walks a Python AST for
  `execute` / `executemany` / `raw` / `execute_sql` and its own manifest scopes it "python stack only".
  Bun's sinks are `bun:sqlite` (`query` / `run` / `exec` / `prepare`), `Bun.sql` and the postgres/mysql
  clients. Realized by `bun_security_hygiene_detector` (core alias SECURITY-SQL-INJECTION-001).

statement: >-
  The object literal passed to an emit-like call naming a declared tracking-plan item MUST NOT
  carry a property the plan forbids on that item (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every concrete telemetry item an acceptance requires MUST be bound to at least one non-test
  implementation source file by a `// Telemetry:` header (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  An emit-like call (emit, emitted, track, capture, record, logEvent, emitEvent, sendEvent) whose
  first argument is a string literal naming an event MUST name an item declared in the tracking
  plan (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  A `// Telemetry:` reference in implementation source names a concrete telemetry URN that resolves
  to a tracking-plan item under the telemetry root (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  A layered source file outside the integration layer and infrastructure directories MUST NOT
  import a telemetry vendor SDK (REQUIRED).

statement: An app component (`.tsx`/`.jsx` outside the design root) MUST render interactive controls through a design-system
  primitive rather than a raw `<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>`, or `<textarea>`, so controls stay themed, accessible,
  and consistent. The same obligation covers controls authored as HTML in the bodies of string, template, and
  tagged-template literals in `.ts`/`.mts` files outside the design root — the shape an htmx/Bun server-rendered
  app writes. Bun realization of `coder.design.primitives`, mirroring `coder.vite.design-primitives`.

statement: Outside the tokens layer, a UI file (`.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.css`) MUST NOT write a raw color
  literal — `#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()` — in a CSS declaration, a `style` attribute,
  a `<style>` block, a JSX `style={{…}}` object, or a `fill`/`stroke`/`bgcolor` attribute. The same declarations are
  judged in inline `style="…"` attributes and `<style>` text authored in the HTML a `.ts`/`.mts` file renders from
  string/template/tagged-template literals. Colors come from tokens (`var(--…)`). Bun realization of
  `coder.design.token-color`, mirroring `coder.vite.design-token-color`.

statement: Outside the tokens layer, a UI file MUST NOT hardcode a spacing, inset, or border-radius length greater
  than 1px (`margin`, `padding`, `gap`, `inset`, `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`, `border-radius`), nor a non-zero
  duration in `transition`/`animation`. A bare number in a JSX style object for those properties counts as a length.
  The same declarations are judged in inline `style="…"` attributes and `<style>` text authored in the HTML a
  `.ts`/`.mts` file renders from string/template/tagged-template literals. These values come from foundations
  tokens. Bun realization of `coder.design.token-hardcoded` and of the raw-pixel part of `coder.design.foundations`.

statement: A code file in the `tokens` or `foundations` layer MUST contain only values — palette, spacing, radii,
  motion, scales — and MUST NOT import a renderer (`hono/jsx`, `react`, `preact`, `@kitajs/html`), render markup,
  or branch with `if`/`for`/`while`/`switch`. Bun realization of `coder.design.foundations` (the bottom of the hierarchy
  is pure), mirroring `coder.vite.design-tokens-pure`.

statement: Each acceptance section declares an abstract Gherkin narrative (given.abstract, when.abstract,
  then.abstract) — all three are REQUIRED.

statement: Bind each acceptance to one metric, respect the parent DESIRED OUTCOME's single dimension/lens, and collocate
  DESIRED OUTCOME + acceptances + tests + artifacts.

statement: Controlled vocabulary of named integration surfaces an acceptance exercises; unknown values
  are rejected.

statement: execution_kind is an orthogonal runtime-environment classifier (live infrastructure vs hermetic),
  separate from harness/category.
statement: Missing context is obtained by asking the user directly — no inference, no suggestions.

statement: The authoring prompt for composing each acceptance field (id, urn, harness, route, given, when,
  then).

statement: given declares only required preconditions; when declares the single harness-specific trigger
  (REQUIRED); then is an array of assertions (REQUIRED).

statement: 'The authoritative harness vocabulary: each harness name maps to an UPPERCASE code and a typical-layer
  catalog entry.'
statement: Each acceptance criterion declares a harness type (UNIT, INTEGRATION, SMOKE, etc.).

statement: When execution_kind is hermetic_integration AND permitted_fakes is non-empty, the acceptance
  MUST declare the hermetic fake-contract block — the declaration IS the contract.
statement: The legacy acceptance id is AC-{STEP}-{NNN} (kept for backward compatibility in identity.id).
statement: Keep acceptances <=5 per DESIRED OUTCOME; if more are needed, split the DESIRED OUTCOME into clearer outcomes.
statement: Keyword cues for selecting the test-layer plane when routing an acceptance.

statement: route.sequence is built as ordered {layer}.{action} transitions flowing presentation -> application
  -> domain -> integration as needed.

statement: Each acceptance declares telemetry signals (metrics, traces, logs, events) using artifact-based
  telemetry URNs (REQUIRED).
statement: An acceptance URN is acc:{capability}:{desired_outcome_id}-{harness}-{NNN}[-{slug}], built via URNBuilder.acceptance.
statement: Each acceptance criterion has Given/When/Then prose and a verifiable outcome.

statement: When creating outputs the planner agent detects, reads, analyzes-by-type,
  and references appendices to enrich outputs; during disambiguation it reads appendices
  to ask grounded clarification questions instead of abstract ones.

statement: Appendix filenames follow the pattern {artifact-name}_{type}_{filename},
  where type is one of the six recognized appendix types.

statement: Appendices are stored in an appendices/ subdirectory of the artifact they
  describe, at the location matching the artifact level (product capability, desired outcome, feature, or
  component).

statement: Appendix sections follow the documented heading order and link back to
  the main product capability body.

statement: An appendix is one of six recognized types — mockup, spreadsheet, document,
  diagram, audio, or video — each with its own file extensions and intended use during
  capability/desired-outcome/feature/component/acceptance creation.

statement: Avoid the catalogued artifact-naming anti-patterns (wrong separator, missing theme, over-specification,
  generic aspect, theme repeated in aspect).

statement: 'The ASPECT (final noun before variant) determines cardinality: a plural aspect indicates a
  collection/array; a singular aspect indicates one item. Categories and variants do not affect cardinality.'

statement: 'Use a colon for hierarchical descent: different conceptual levels, navigating deeper, general->specific,
  organizational subsystems.'

statement: 'An artifact path maps directly to a contract file path: theme + segments become directories,
  the final segment becomes the filename, with a .schema.json extension.'

statement: Keep hierarchy 2-3 levels (4-5 max, sparingly) and variants shallow (0-1 dots, 2 max); each
  separator should add clear semantic value.
statement: 'Use a dot for lateral variation: same conceptual level, different flavor/state/type/facet.'

statement: 'Artifact names (logical) map to contract file paths (physical): split on : and ., each segment
  is a directory level, the final segment is the filename.'

statement: Migrate legacy names to theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant by assigning a theme, separating hierarchy
  (colons) from variants (dots), and realigning URNs, manifests, and contract files.

statement: An artifact name is {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? — theme, optional hierarchy
  categories, a leaf aspect, and an optional variant.

statement: When a produced artifact declares a concrete contract schema file, the
  file path must mirror the identity — every colon/dot boundary becomes a directory
  boundary under contracts/ and the leaf is a .schema.json file
  (contracts/{theme}/.../{aspect}.schema.json). A null contract or a
  directory-reference physical form is out of scope; a mis-located .schema.json is
  a violation.
statement: Planner artifacts use stable URN-based names matching the registered grammar.

statement: Use singular aspect for item schemas and plural aspect for collections, following English pluralization
  rules.

statement: A contract's $id is the clean artifact name {theme}:{resource}[.{category}] with NO 'urn:contract:'
  prefix and NO version suffix; version is a separate top-level field.
statement: Colon means hierarchical descent (unlimited depth); dot means lateral variation (keep shallow).

statement: A produced or consumed artifact/contract identity must be theme-first — it must
  parse as the grammar {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})?, every colon/dot
  token must be kebab-case, and the leading theme must be declared in plan/_themes.yaml.
statement: 'A contract URN exactly matches the artifact name, preserving colons and dots: contract:{artifact_name}.'
statement: Artifact names must satisfy the format, semantic, and technical validation rules.

statement: The product capability and feature names already on disk are scanned for verb-object
  conformance and the non-conforming ones are reported with a count, so naming drift
  is visible and its size is known. This reports; it never blocks.

statement: An artifact is a produced-or-consumed unit of the domain — a theme-namespaced,
  URN-identified thing (material, contract, schema) that product capabilities exchange and that DESIRED OUTCOMES
  and acceptances prove. Its identity follows the canonical naming pattern (theme:hierarchy:aspect.variant)
  and mirrors its declared location. This is a planner domain-decomposition artifact
  naming WHAT is exchanged; its runtime realization as flow variables in flight is a coder/tester
  concern. This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly;
  the enforceable parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes
  that require it.

statement: A product capability's produced artifacts carry a contract URN (contract:{...}) and a telemetry URN (telemetry:{...})
  following the artifact-naming grammar.

statement: Product capability sizing has two orthogonal axes — intrinsic footprint (how much work is inside) and coupling complexity (whether the cut is correct). Complexity is modeled as super-linear in cross-capability coupling, not additive in component count.

statement: Report each product capability's cross-capability coupling complexity (fan_in x fan_out over the produce->consume name graph); flag product capabilities above a soft, config-driven threshold. Advisory and non-blocking.

statement: A product capability is a separable, semantically-coherent unit of work within a journey
  — a single subject/action/goal that consumes and produces declared artifacts and
  composes with sibling product capabilities into user/system flows without forming a produce/consume cycle.
  This is a planner domain-decomposition artifact naming a unit of the domain; how the
  unit executes at runtime is a coder/tester concern. This node is an advisory semantic
  anchor — it enforces nothing directly; the enforceable parts of this meaning are
  decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes that require it.

statement: A product capability's features are declared as an array of URN objects (feature:{capability-slug}:{feature-name});
  the legacy object map is deprecated.
statement: A product capability's _features.yaml lists every feature module and its current status.

statement: Logical identifiers (URNs, slugs, YAML refs) use kebab-case; the filesystem (directories, manifest
  files, feature files) uses snake_case.

statement: A product capability slug must be verb-object — kebab-case, at least two tokens, the
  leading token a verb from the convention verb lexicon, and no connective tokens.
  Brand or proper-noun slugs must be listed explicitly in capability.convention.yaml
  verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions; an implicit exception is a violation.
statement: The directed product capability graph built from produce->consume artifact NAMES must be acyclic; no strongly-connected component may span more than one product capability.

statement: produce[] entries declare name + contract + telemetry (optional to/urn/version); consume[]
  entries declare name (optional from/contract/telemetry/urn/version).

statement: Refine ambiguous input into a structured product capability by extracting subject, action, goal, context,
  outcome, produce/consume artifacts, and theme.

statement: 'A product capability must be semantically coherent: subject/action/goal align, outcome is measurable, produce
  is owned, consume is foreign, and at least one produce is external.'

statement: A product capability should be separable — its internal cohesion (intra-capability shared-token DESIRED OUTCOME edges) at least its tightest coupling to any single neighbor product capability. A product capability more bound to a neighbor than to itself emits a [MERGE] signal. Advisory and non-blocking.
statement: Convert between logical slugs and filesystem names by swapping hyphens and underscores.

statement: 'A telemetry URN maps to a filesystem directory of signal files: telemetry:{theme}:{segments}
  -> telemetry/{theme}/{segments}/{signal-type}.{plane}[.{measure}].json.'
statement: A product capability URN is capability:{kebab-case-name}, preferring a verb-object slug; built via URNBuilder.capability.
statement: Product capabilities declare a stable URN and live under plan/<capability-slug>/ with the documented file layout.

statement: Component names are derived from artifact resources by converting the resource
  to PascalCase and adding a capability suffix chosen by the artifact type (events,
  states, data, configs).

statement: Each component must have a single business capability, and its name must
  reflect that primary business purpose.

statement: A feature must have at most 8 components; beyond 8 indicates the feature
  is too large and should be split.

statement: Components are derived from feature analysis — from ioSeeds triggers (events,
  commands, queries) and from DESIRED OUTCOME verbs (validate, process, display, persist, coordinate)
  — each trigger generating a component with a business capability and layer.

statement: A component's consumed and produced events must be a subset of the owning
  feature's ioSeeds; every event must be traceable to a feature ioSeed.

statement: A component is assigned to an architectural layer based on its artifact
  type and responsibility, using the typical-layer mapping for events, states, data,
  and configs.

statement: A component belongs to exactly one architectural layer, and its URN must
  contain a valid layer value.

statement: A component must have at most 5 methods; split the component if more methods
  are needed.

statement: A generated component carries a complete structure — URN, required parent
  feature, templated description, consumed/produced events (max 3 each), and dependencies.

statement: The canonical component type catalog enumerates every component type by
  side (backend|frontend), layer, file suffix per language, description, and complexity
  weight, derived from the coder backend/frontend conventions.

statement: Every contract URN on a product capability produce/consume must resolve to a contract registered in contracts/_contracts.yaml; no cross-capability produce/consume edge may carry contract null; every produced contract must have a consumer or be explicitly marked external.

statement: >-
  Operative prose in a convention node — the fix_hint, operational_guidance,
  normative_text, statement and term text a reader is expected to ACT on — must
  name only files that exist in the repo and only CLI verbs that still resolve.
  A fix_hint is an executable promise: if it names a file, that file must be
  there; if it names a verb, that verb must run.
statement: A product capability and its features must reference each other bidirectionally (feature->product capability and product capability->feature).
statement: A user/system flow and its product capabilities must reference each other bidirectionally (product capability->user/system flow and user/system flow->product capability).

statement: 'The planner coverage graph ensures traceability from user/system flows down to acceptances: user/system flow ->
  Product capability -> Feature -> DESIRED OUTCOME -> Acceptance, each level guarded by coverage validators.'
statement: Every DESIRED OUTCOME must be referenced by at least one feature (desired outcome->feature).
statement: Every DESIRED OUTCOME must have at least one acceptance criterion (except status:draft).

statement: Coverage exceptions are declared via config allow-lists and status exemptions (draft artifacts
  are exempt from 2.1 and 2.4).

statement: Acceptance given sections default to empty auth scopes, no builders, no time, strict stubbing
  policy, and no knobs.
statement: Reusable given/when/then scaffolding template per harness, with the layers it typically exercises.

statement: Each DESIRED OUTCOME dimension+direction maps to a default metric_id (e.g. time/minimize -> metric:latency_p50), or is explicitly declared unmapped. The table is total over desired-outcome.schema.json's dimension x direction enums; nothing falls through it silently.
statement: Keyword cues route an acceptance to a layer plane (presentation, application, domain, integration).

statement: 'Each layer maps to a default action in the route sequence: presentation.command, application.use_case,
  domain.validate, integration.persist.'
statement: 'Criteria entries follow the documented shape: id, description, harness, and expected_outcome.'

statement: 'Job steps use the canonical step vocabulary owned by steps.convention:
  Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude. This
  protocol references those steps; it does not re-enumerate or redefine them.'

statement: Each product capability's description must make its capability boundary understandable
  later without the original conversation. It uses the existing product capability schema description
  field; no new field is introduced.

statement: "If the agent cannot adequately parse, analyze, or review a source document,\
  \ it must inform the operator \u2014 stating what it could not extract or understand\
  \ and asking how to proceed \u2014 rather than planning from a partial reading."

statement: Plan decomposes what the system does (user-facing jobs), not how it is
  built. Implementation-flavored sources are reframed to user-facing jobs or routed
  to tests/ADRs (e.g. 'use redis for caching' becomes 'browse catalog pages with instant
  response').

statement: 'Keep two grammars separate: the main job uses JTBD job-statement grammar
  (verb + object + contextual clarifier); DESIRED OUTCOMES use ODI outcome grammar (direction
  + dimension + object_of_control + context_clarifier). Collapsing job into outcome
  too early produces malformed plan/.'

statement: 'Decomposition advances by per-unit keep/pivot/kill: the operator keeps,
  pivots (names a modification), or kills each candidate (heuristic, analog, main
  job, product capability, feature, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance); an artifact is written only after a final-granularity
  keep.'

statement: 'Each invocation targets a scoped slice; different runs have different
  framing. The agent reads existing plan/ via the repo graph to compose, and does
  not inherit prior-run framing. What is NOT in this protocol: no atdd agent ask,
  no step-1 disk persistence, no plan/_meta.yaml, no coach involvement.'

statement: The operator may answer in prose; the agent normalizes the reply to keep/pivot/kill
  (plus a named modification for pivot). If the interpretation is ambiguous, the agent
  restates its interpretation and confirms before proceeding.

statement: 'After product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES are kept, decode the journey: the nominal user/system flow
  (the main-job journey) plus operator keep/pivot/kill on error, alternate, and exception
  sibling user/system flows. Absorbs the retired PLAN-3B (#940).'

statement: Every core planner domain artifact (theme, user/system flow, flow router, product capability, feature, desired outcome, artifact) MUST have a `planner.<artifact>.definition` advisory semantic anchor node (kind family) that is graph-connected — appearing as a source_ref or target_ref of at least one edge in the relationship graph. A missing or non-family or orphan anchor is refused.

statement: Declare a context clarifier — a detailed situational phrase specifying when/where/how the DESIRED OUTCOME
  applies (required, one line).

statement: A DESIRED OUTCOME (What Must Be True) is a falsifiable statement of a single outcome
  that must hold for an artifact — scoped to one object of control along one dimension,
  direction, and lens — declared with an id and a statement, and paired with the
  acceptances that prove it, including at least one smoke acceptance. This node is an advisory semantic
  anchor — it enforces nothing directly; the enforceable parts of this meaning are
  decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes that require it.

statement: Select exactly one optimization dimension (the core metric the user wants to optimize) for
  a DESIRED OUTCOME.
statement: Select the optimization direction verb that matches the goal, from the controlled palette.
statement: A DESIRED OUTCOME file is named {STEP_CODE}{NNN}.yaml — step-coded, no prefix.
statement: Select one quality lens (social, functional, or emotional) most relevant to the work.

statement: Every DESIRED OUTCOME must declare at least one acceptance URN with the SMOKE harness token (acc:<capability>:<desired_outcome_id>-SMOKE-NNN[-<slug>])
  so the lifecycle has explicit real-infrastructure coverage before REFACTOR.
statement: Synthesize the specific thing being controlled or manipulated as a kebab-case noun phrase.
statement: A DESIRED OUTCOME entry declares its id, its statement, and the artifacts that prove the statement.

statement: Keep <=5 acceptances per DESIRED OUTCOME; split on mixed dimensions, multiple actors, or divergent gates;
  keep together for single-truth-multiple-layers or a coherent sequence.
statement: 'A DESIRED OUTCOME statement is composed as: {direction} {dimension} of {object_of_control} [context_clarifier].'
statement: The single-letter step codes (D L P C E M Y R K) that prefix a DESIRED OUTCOME sequence.

statement: A DESIRED OUTCOME URN is desired-outcome:{capability}:{STEP_CODE}{NNN} — a unique step-coded identifier built via URNBuilder.desiredOutcome(capability_id,
  sequence).

statement: >-
  `docs/architecture/decisions/index.adoc` MUST list exactly the ADRs the corpus declares, derived
  from their `:decides:` edges. An ADR present in the tree and absent from the registry — or listed
  in the registry and absent from the tree — is a violation. The registry is a projection, never a
  typed list (spec 2 §5.2, §6).

  WHAT COUNTS AS A LISTING. Where the registry declares a machine-maintained region —
  `// BEGIN GENERATED: adr-register` … `// END GENERATED: adr-register`, the markers a generator
  writes around its own output — only that region is read. A corpus whose generator marks its
  output has already said where its list begins and ends, and taking it at its
